subject: Throughput degradation on NorthBridge VPC - urgent action plan
messages:
From: ops@northbridge.ai
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: dave.cto@northbridge.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 07:32:00 -0400
Subject: Sudden throughput collapse in private cluster (prod-us-east)

Hi Rachel,

We're seeing a sustained throughput drop and a spike in 500s from our private deployment in prod-us-east starting ~06:45 ET. QPS down ~65%, p95 latency increasing from 120ms to ~1.2s. Error traces in the app show repeated tokenization/KV read timeouts. Cost impact is material — several customer-critical flows are timing out.

We opened a ticket (INC-7231) and attached a small perf snapshot and recent logs. Can Redwood triage? We need an initial assessment and ETA for mitigation. Our CTO (Dave) asked me to escalate to someone who can coordinate with eng and execs.

Attachments: perf_dump_20270421.tar.gz (log bundle), kvcache_snapshot_0421.bin (kv snapshot)

Thanks,
Sanjay Kumar
Head of Platform Ops
NorthBridge AI
From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: ops@northbridge.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 07:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse in private cluster (prod-us-east)

Sanjay — thanks for the quick flag. I see INC-7231 and downloading the bundle now. Initial ask: can you confirm whether any recent model or weight changes were pushed in the last 24h, and if you have a short list of queries that reproduce the 500s?

Immediate plan (high-level):
- I'll run a sanity pass on KV cache integrity with our infra team (Vivek copied).
- Bring in a runtime engineer to look for kernel/quantization regressions (Marissa copied).
- If we need a short-term mitigation we'll put a temporary routing policy to a compatible fallback model variant to recover QPS while we debug.

I'll update within 60 minutes with findings and proposed mitigation. If Dave is available for a quick sync, propose 08:30 ET.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Sales Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops@northbridge.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse in private cluster (prod-us-east)

Looping in a few quick observations from the initial KV snapshot:
- Several shard-level KV lookup latencies jump past 200ms intermittently; looks like sustained lock contention on node-3.
- Node-3 is showing elevated GPU MEM utilization plus CMS swapping events in kernel logs.
- No model weight change found in the last 48h from the snapshot metadata.

Immediate suggestions:
1) Drain traffic off node-3 and rebalance shard placement,
2) Enable temporary routing to the nearest compatible variant (quantized) for best-effort recovery,
3) Collect a longer perf profile for 30 minutes with tracing enabled (I can kick this off but need permission from NorthBridge ops to increase trace sampling).

I'll prepare a short runbook for draining/rebalance and the fallback switch — sending in a separate doc.

—Vivek
VP, Runtime Reliability
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: ops@northbridge.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse in private cluster (prod-us-east)

Bringing in specifics for the runbook and timeline. Summary:
- T0 (08:30 ET): Have NorthBridge ops accept temporary traffic steering.
- T0+5m: Apply routing policy to divert 30-50% of traffic to quantized-compat variant in same region (minimal model change required).
- T0+10m: Drain node-3 by cordoning and shifting KV shards; monitor p95 and 500 rate.
- T0+30m: Assess recovery; if QPS still <80% of baseline, increase diversion to 70% and escalate to canary rollback of recent infra config (if any).

I'll attach the runbook. Risks: short-term quality delta using a quantized variant, potential cold-cache penalty during shard move.

Attachments: nb-incident-action-plan-v1.docx

—Marissa
Head, Runtime Engineering
From: ops@northbridge.ai
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: dave.cto@northbridge.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:35:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse in private cluster (prod-us-east)

Thanks — we approve the temporary routing and runbook. Dave can do the 08:30 ET sync. We have a scheduled maintenance window later tonight at 23:00 ET but prefer to avoid if we can recover earlier.

Quick note from our side: there was an autoscaler patch applied two nights ago but our change logs show it was a config flag for cooldown; we did not change model binaries. Will share the exact diff after the sync.

—Sanjay
From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: dave.cto@northbridge.ai, ops@northbridge.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 18:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse in private cluster (prod-us-east) — post-mitigation summary for execs

Dave / Sanjay — following the mitigation runbook:
- 08:35 ET: diverted 40% traffic to quantized-compat variant; p95 improved from ~1.2s to ~320ms within 6 minutes.
- 08:45 ET: drained node-3 and rebalanced shards; QPS recovered to ~92% baseline by 08:55 ET.
- Root cause (preliminary): autoscaler cooldown flag change resulted in delayed eviction behavior + a GC pattern that exposed a kernel-level mem fragmentation on node-3. No model weight change.
- Next steps:
  * Immediate: We'll keep 30% traffic on fallback variant during your evening peak (until midnight ET) and maintain elevated tracing.
  * Short-term (48h): plan maintenance to repro the issue in staging with the autoscaler config diff + mem-pressure tests; run targeted kernel upgrade on node-3 image if reproduced.
  * Exec ask: approval to schedule a rolling kernel patch for the cluster during the 23:00 ET window (estimated 45–60 minutes impact with controlled drain).

I've attached the action plan and logs for your SRE/infra review. Please confirm approval for the rolling kernel patch so we can lock a time.

—Rachel
Sales Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
Rachel.Kim@redwood.com
